scope: Paired scratch graphics-GPU scatter and owned QImage readback; no application backend.
limits: Scratch-only persistent-buffer/QImage experiment; no application renderer or preferences changed.
GPU timing includes point preparation, uploads, dispatch and owned QImage readback. CPU and GPU are paired in alternating order on identical native-sized material inputs.
Only the default spaCR palette with zero dot flicker and no colour-wave event is in this first experiment; no random-palette or full native-widget acceptance claimed.
Other agents are active on CPU; these measurements alone do not establish production speedup.
Persistent buffers and direct owned QImage readback do not establish an acceleration benefit.
No default GPU switch or production graphics backend is justified by this result.
CPU agent activity and repeated immutable material inputs constrain interpretation; pixel equality is scoped to these exact inputs.
